outcomeNote: A mishna stating law; no named parties, no dispute and no dialectical move in the unit, so no interactions are emitted.

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ בְּהֵמָה שֶׁנֶּחְתְּכוּ רַגְלֶיהָ מִן הָאַרְכּוּבָּה וּלְמַטָּה – כְּשֵׁרָה, מִן הָאַרְכּוּבָּה וּלְמַעְלָה – פְּסוּלָה, וְכֵן שֶׁנִּיטַּל צוֹמֶת הַגִּידִין.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» With regard to «an animal whose hind legs were severed,» if they were severed «from the leg joint and below,» the animal is «kosher; from the leg joint and above,» the animal is thereby rendered a tereifa and is «not kosher. And likewise,» an animal «whose convergence of sinews» in the thigh «was removed» is a tereifa and is not kosher.

segments.he: נִשְׁבַּר הָעֶצֶם, אִם רוֹב הַבָּשָׂר קַיָּים – שְׁחִיטָתוֹ מְטַהַרְתּוֹ, וְאִם לָאו – אֵין שְׁחִיטָתוֹ מְטַהַרְתּוֹ.
segments.en: If «the bone» of a limb «was broken» but the limb was not completely severed, and the animal was then slaughtered, «if the majority of the flesh» surrounding the bone «is intact, the slaughter of» the animal «renders it permitted; but if not, its slaughter does not render it permitted.»

moves.summary: the mishna fixes the leg joint as the line between a kosher animal and a tereifa, and adds the convergence of sinews
where the bone is broken but the limb not severed, slaughter permits it only if most of the flesh remains
